answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No 22-miler, and you do not need one. The race is two weekends away, so Sunday Oct 4 is the last long run that can actually train you; anything after that is taper and just recovers the legs. A 22 this Sunday would leave you walking into race day still digesting it, and a 22 the Sunday before the race is flat-out a bad idea.

Here is the better trade: run 20 mi on Sunday with the last 6 mi at marathon pace (around 8:35/mi). That gives you more race-specific work than a slow 22 would, confirms the pace feels controlled, and still lets you taper cleanly. You already have a 20 in the bank from Sep 13 and a strong 17 last week at 9:59/mi and HR 146 — the aerobic base is there. Trust it.

new.analysis:
## Why this week looks like this

This is your peak week, and the long run is the whole point of it. Everything else is built to leave you fresh for Sunday, because that session is your last chance to rehearse marathon pace on tired legs before Oct 18.

The Wednesday session steps down from threshold to marathon pace on purpose. You have plenty of threshold work in your legs from the last three weeks, and what you need now is to groove 8:35/mi so it feels automatic on race day. Keep it honest but not strained — if the pace feels like a 7/10 effort, that is right.

I am keeping weekly volume near last week at around 44 mi. No jumps now; your body needs to arrive at the start line absorbing fitness, not building it. The Saturday strides are just to keep the legs snappy before Sunday, not a workout.

About the anxiety: it is normal, and the plan is designed so you do not have to make big decisions in the next 20 days. Follow the lines, sleep, eat, and show up. The fitness is already built.
